observations: Revision 3 is selected; revision 2 operand stacks are superseded and retained only for comparison.
The system uses principal-pair num/op2/op1/dup/era rules; arithmetic takes two semantic interactions, preserving first-minus-second subtraction.
The documented K = 2*ops + dups + eras is a semantic claim, not a measured native counter or proof of the documented lowering.
The Noble whitelist also includes equality and ordered multiple outputs. Lattice still admits only two I64 inputs, one I64 output and Input/Const/Add/Sub/Mul.

The current source now supplies a sequential Rust net reducer and actual noble ngraph eval GRAPH VECTORS --net [--fuel N] entry point. This supersedes the older 23e529 snapshot's missing-runtime observation.

net::Limits has max_agent_slots, max_wires and interaction_fuel only; retained_bytes is an estimate, not an enforced whole-request allocation/memory ceiling. The CLI uses default agent/wire limits and a tightened fuel, with no admitted byte-ceiling field.
selected_producer_contract.executable: noble (source target only; no measured executable artifact selected)
selected_producer_contract.worker_schema: noble-ngraph-report/v1 (CLI JSON-lines transport, not yet admitted as a Lattice worker protocol)

runtime_source_observations.observation: Real lower/validate/reduce implementation, exact contract/lowering identities, fuel/agent/wire caps, agent-derived bounded worklist, cancellation callback and complete-only readback. Limits exposes no independent allocation/memory or output-construction byte ceiling; Report.retained_bytes estimates initial net storage, not total consumption.

Actual --net route lowers and reduces fresh nets. eval_net reports graph/backend/vector/outputs/interactions/peak_live_agents/final_wires/retained_bytes, but no theorem, native-counter correspondence, executable digest or enclosing Lattice attempt binding. Reports are buffered in a growing Vec before stdout; a host stdout cap is not a producer output-construction memory ceiling.

The previously unavailable module is now landed. It defines system with proved rule_wf/rule_symm, i64_normal_form_unique, i64_equal_interaction_count and Certificate.accepted_exact_count. Source inspection only, no proof replay. i64_equal_interaction_count explicitly assumes a canonical complete reduction of the formula length as well as the alternative complete reduction; it is not an unconditional Rust theorem.

theorems_inspected.name: Rewriting.StrongConfluent.normal_unique
theorems_inspected.hypotheses: Invariant preservation and one-step diamond; invariant initial state; two finite reductions from that same state; normality of both endpoints.
theorems_inspected.conclusion: Equal endpoints and complete reduction lengths.

theorems_inspected.name: INet.normal_form_unique
theorems_inspected.hypotheses: INet.System with rule_wf and rule_symm; well-formed initial net; two Step reductions with normal endpoints.
theorems_inspected.conclusion: Equal normal forms and semantic principal-pair interaction counts.

theorems_inspected.name: INet.reduction_bounded
theorems_inspected.hypotheses: Same system and well-formed initial net; supplied reduction to a normal form; another reduction prefix.
theorems_inspected.conclusion: Prefix length no greater than supplied normalization length, and extension to that normal form.

theorems_inspected.name: NobleFoundation.NetI64.i64_equal_interaction_count
theorems_inspected.hypotheses: translateChecked succeeds; canonical CStep reduction has program.interactionCount steps and a normal endpoint; alternative CStep reduction from that same source reaches a normal endpoint.
theorems_inspected.conclusion: Alternative normal form equals canonical normal form and its step count equals program.interactionCount. Native runtime correspondence is not a hypothesis supplied by this declaration.
